proposals.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (about 6 eV), electronically insulating lithium-ion conductor. It is chemically compatible with sulfide Li6PS5Cl and is oxidatively stable up to about 4 V, so it should act as a low-penalty interlayer between LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte. As a Li-rich orthophosphate it should also have little reactivity with either side.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (about 6 eV), electronically insulating lithium-ion conductor. It is chemically compatible with sulfide Li6PS5Cl and is oxidatively stable up to about 4 V, so it should act as a low-penalty interlayer between LiCoO2 and the sulfide electrolyte. As a Li-rich orthophosphate it should also have little reactivity with either side.

LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-rich fluoride. Fluoride anions are poor reductants and form strongly bonded LiF, so reduction of the sulfide by LiF should be less favorable than for the phosphate. A thin LiF interlayer should block electron transfer between LiCoO2 and Li6PS5Cl with a smaller contact penalty than Li3PO4, which released P2O5, SO2 and SCl4 on contact.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 was insulating and wide-gap but had a high contact penalty (0.337 eV/non-Li atom, bin 16) from decomposition products with the sulfide, so the next choice moves to a different family with a more inert anion.
